claim: Code contamination extends beyond exact/near-exact duplication to include 'Shared Logic' cases -- semantically equivalent but textually different solutions -- which surface-level deduplication and matching pipelines fail to detect.
stance_target: surface-level string-matching decontamination checks being sufficient to certify a code benchmark as uncontaminated
scope_conditions: 3 widely used code benchmarks, 3 representative post-training datasets; submitted May 2026
quoted_support: TRACER models contamination using three levels of semantic overlap - Functionally Identical, Nearly Identical, and Shared Logic - and detects them through a coarse-to-fine pipeline.

claim: A semantic-aware contamination detector (TRACER) achieves F1=0.91 for fine-grained contamination detection and F1=0.92 for binary detection using GPT-5 as backbone, outperforming existing contamination-detection methods by 42-217%.
stance_target: feasibility and performance ceiling of automated semantic contamination detection for code LLM benchmarks
scope_conditions: evaluated across multiple LLM backbones; GPT-5 as best-performing backbone
quoted_support: TRACER achieves strong and consistent performance across multiple LLM backbones, with GPT-5 reaching an F1 score of 0.91 in fine-grained detection. In the binary setting, TRACER attains an F1 of 0.92, outperforming existing methods by 42%-217%.
